Mercedes Recalls A-Class Through GLC Line Over Faulty Door Lock Microswitches
69 photos
Photo: Mercedes-Benz
Mercedes-Benz AG has a bit of a problem with a component many drivers never even think about until their cars refuse to engage the electronic parking brake. A microswitch inside the driver's door lock can stop recognizing when someone opens the door if enough moisture builds up in there, compromising the auto-park function as well.
Per the State Administration for Market Regulation, the Stuttgart-based automaker is recalling a whopping 180,277 vehicles over this defect in the People's Republic of China. This recall actually consists of two separate campaigns. Beijing Mercedes-Benz Automotive is listed with 129,819 locally assembled models, while the second campaign targets 50,458 imported vehicles.
Beijing Mercedes-Benz Automotive lists production dates between February 8, 2018, and June 1, 2020, for the locally produced A-Class, GLA, and GLB . The other population comprises the A-, B-, and C-Class, CLA, CLE, GLA, GLC, and GLC lines, with production dates ranging from April 21, 2018, through February 25, 2026. In both cases, the affected driver's door lock assemblies will be replaced from February 2027 onward.
The microswitch's potting material is the weak point, allowing water to get in there. Insufficient resistance to moisture results in a corroded electrical switch. In this state, the vehicle may no longer correctly recognize if the driver has opened or closed the door. Because the electronic parking brake and auto-park function rely on that information, both functions could malfunction.
This is not Merc's first microswitch rodeo, though. Back in July 2026, the company recalled no fewer than 310,667 such vehicles in the United States of America under NHTSA campaign 26V481. Affected models included the A-Class, CLA, C-Class, GLA, GLB, and the GLC to boot. Instead of repairing the microswitch, dealers were instructed to fully replace the door lock assembly.
Photo: Mercedes-Benz Australia followed suit with campaign REC-006695 in August 2026, covering just under 59,000 vehicles from the 2018 through 2026 model years. The local regulator described the very same vulnerability and safety risks.
In addition to said microswitch recall, the German automaker has also identified a problem that affects only two electric CLAs produced in China for the Chinese market. Assembled by Beijing Mercedes-Benz on November 25, 2026, and December 3, 2026, said models are suspected of damaged electrical components on the circuit board inside the rear drive module's power electronics unit.
A potential electrical short may interrupt power transmission, and you clearly don't want such a loss of motive power when driving at high speeds. These vehicles will have their affected modules replaced at no charge to affected customers. Also worth noting, both CLAs qualify for immediate attention.
Waiting until February 2027 for the scheduled campaign to begin in China is understandable, but only just. Considering that 180,277 vehicles have to be inspected, Merc's local subsidiary must stock up on replacement door lock assemblies efficiently in only a few short months.
The logistical effort is massive, and replacing so many door locks definitely takes a lot of time. In the meantime, potentially affected customers may get in touch with Beijing Mercedes-Benz Automobile and Mercedes-Benz Automobile Sales by phone for additional information regarding parts availability.

Korean Air Aerospace Division's LOWUS Collaborative Combat Aircraft (Photo: Korean Air)
DAEJEON, South Korea — Korean Air Aerospace Division (KE-ASD) is readying its Low Observable Wingman Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle System (LOWUS) loyal wingman drone to make its first flight by the end of this year, the company has announced .
During a visit to KE-ASD’s research and development facility in South Korea at the end of October, executives briefed media on the research and development activities conducted by the specialized aerospace and defense manufacturing business unit of Korean Air airline. That included discussing LOWUS, which the company plans to enter as its contender for South Korea’s upcoming Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) competition.
Like other media outlets, Breaking Defense accepted travel and accommodations from KE-ASD to attend the briefing.
“We delivered our CCA platform last year and will having flight tests at the end of this year,” Director of International Business for KE-ASD Haneul Kim confirmed, adding that that two technology demonstrator aircraft have been handed over to South Korea’s Agency for Defense Development (ADD).
Following the initial trials, LOWUS, which has a length of 10.4 meters (34.1 feet) and a wingspan of 9.4 meters, will enter a full-scale development program that is due to begin in 2029 to meet the anticipated South Korean government’s timeline for the CCA competition . The Korean government has not indicated when the competition will start, but the eventual CCA winner is expected to be deployed alongside manned platforms and later production blocks of the KF-21 fighter.
A 5,500-lbf turbofan engine being developed by the ADD and Hanwha is expected to be ready in 2032 for use with the LOWUS, enabling the CCA to fly at speeds of up to Mach 0.8 and stay aloft for up to three hours. This will replace the Ukrainian AI-222 engine that is powering the initial aircraft.
Jung told reporters that LOWUS will be equipped with an Active Electronically Scanned Array Radar and Electro Optical systems, with its initial mission set being reconnaissance and eventually expanded to include penetrating contested airspace ahead of manned aircraft for strike and other combat missions.
AI Pilot Program
On the software front, ADD has launched a project to develop an AI Pilot that will have AI-enabled air combat technologies, and Jung added that there are plans to retrofit and integrate the system into the LOWUS aircraft currently under development for flight demonstration.
KE-ASD has also invested significant effort into the development of AI-enabled drone swarm software, with the company successfully demonstrating its efforts in September at the 2026 Defense Drone Tech Fair in South Korea.
“A fleet of 22 drones autonomously carried out coordinated reconnaissance, high-maneuver swarm flight and precision strike missions, managed through Korean Air’s proprietary integrated battle management system,” said a KE-ASD social media post about the September demonstration.
Video from the event showed 22 drones moving into two separate swarms, with one acting as decoys to occupy a simulated adversary air defense system while the other swarm conducted an attack against a preset target by crashing into it in rapid succession.
“The system does more than provide voice updates based on a pre-set scenario: it uses AI to assess mission status in real time and communicate relevant updates. It can also retrieve drone status and weather information in response to user queries, making it optimized for operations in the field,” the post added.
KE-ASD’s Senior Manager for Systems Integration Sumno Jung said the technology demonstrators will be used for the flight tests which will then lead to Manned-Unmanned Teaming (MUM-T) trials with an ADD-operated KT-1 turboprop trainer that is scheduled to begin at the end of 2027.

source_document.body:
Renewable energy must overcome significant challenges, and if it succeeds, it can achieve the potential that many envision. Renewable energy must be ever-economical and ever-competitive. Otherwise, it will continue to lag. Ideology never got a megawatt-hour (MWh) to market; economic competitiveness did.
COMMENTARY
To set the stage, we know that generation using fossil fuels is less capital intensive (per MW of capacity and per MWh of energy), enough so that non-renewable energy can afford to purchase and consume fossil fuels and still generate profits for its owners. Fossil generators make money. That is why people build them. Like it or not, fossil fuel generation is economically competitive and generally requires less capital per MW of capacity and per MWh of energy than renewables. That is the big economic hurdle that renewable energy needs to clear if it is to grow substantially. It has in a number of venues, and it can into the future.
The way renewables generators approach the problem is potentially a productive one. Historically, the energy system has been a combustion-driven system. You get a hydrocarbon (or coal, an almost pure carbon) out of the crust of the earth, refine it, and burn it in oxygen, creating heat that is turned into electricity or kinetic energy (in cars, trucks, planes, and power plants). They can run 98% of the time, and some can be black started to follow load. They are constant, not intermittent. The carbon and hydrogen in the initial fuel go into the atmosphere as CO 2 and water vapor. CO 2 is what we strive to avoid. One hundred-plus years of research and operation have brought these techniques to a fairly advanced state. And now we are looking for a sea change.
The way to understand the sea change potential of renewables is that we are trying to move from a “combustion economy” to a “solid-state economy.” A solid-state economy is one in which we don’t “burn stuff” in the atmosphere but rather rely on advanced electrical and solid-state and material science methodologies, most of which are not yet with us, economically speaking. Electric cars or large wind turbines with heat-resistant magnets, or uUltra-high-capacity batteries that exploit new chemistry and materials science. Transportation power sources that do not release CO 2 from mobile platforms but rather eject zero combustion products. Fuel cells that do not cost an arm and a leg.
If we do “burn stuff,” we want to do so in things like fuel cells that do not let the products of combustion enter into the atmosphere at all and can use just about any combustible. We need advanced technologies that can exploit nuclear and atomic structures, like fission or maybe even fusion power. (Incredibly, and laudably, Lawrence Livermore National Lab achieved “ignition” in its laser fusion developments in the past year or two. Breeder reactors are a well-known, but controversial, technology. These are the epitome of materials science problems that need to be made to work economically and accepted publicly. Reactors are with us today; the economics and regulations are not.)
The solution for renewable energy is not ideology or regulation. It is technology. It is economics. It is pricing. It is capital. It is getting the critical materials out of the ground to build renewable generation and associated control and delivery technologies. The largest challenge we face as an industry is getting the capital to deploy to develop and implement advanced technologies. In part, we have a “mining problem”: getting the advanced materials that are needed to affect the materials science solution rather than the combustion solution. The combustion economy required us to drill for trapped hydrocarbons. The solid-state economy requires us to mine for concentrated critical materials (called “ores”), often in difficult places around the world.
The author has developed a number of power plants in North America and has modeled the electrical system to know their profitability. Investors must know that their renewables plants will be profitable or they will not invest in them.
— Dale M. Nesbitt is president of ArrowHead Economics . He can be reached at dale.nesbitt@arrowheadeconomics.com .

source_document.body:
Full data from the Phase 3 HORIZON trial of Novartis’ pelacarsen failed to show any apparent benefit, leading analysts to further reduce the odds of success for Lp(a)-lowering competitors such as Amgen’s olpasiran.
After Novartis and Ionis Pharmaceuticals reported that pelacarsen failed to improve cardiovascular outcomes in a late-stage test, analysts had held out hope that the details would still leave some room for other therapies that target Lp(a). But now, with the fine print revealed, industry watchers see a tough path ahead for the space.
“HORIZON’s full data offer little silver lining,” Truist Securities analysts said in a Sunday evening note.
While the antisense oligonucleotide greatly lowered levels of lipoprotein(a)—aka, the bad cholesterol—HORIZON found no benefit in terms of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), according to the company’s presentation at the 2026 American Heart Association Scientific Sessions on Saturday and a simultaneous publication in The New England Journal of Medicine ( NEJM ). The trial featured 8,300 adults with cardiovascular disease who were followed for seven years.
Investors had been focused on the full HORIZON dataset for possible trends pointing toward a benefit in cardiovascular outcomes “that could have read-through to ongoing trials with siRNA and oral molecules that have greater Lp(a) lowering capacity,” William Blair analysts wrote in a Monday morning note, but “HORIZON cut many ways remains negative.”
Among patients with high Lp(a), a MACE event—which includes nonfatal heart attack, stroke, an urgent revascularization procedure to open clogged heart arteries or death from any cardiovascular cause—occurred in 380 participants (9.1%) treated with pelacarsen compared to 434 participants (10.4%) on placebo, according to a subgroup analysis published in NEJM Evidence .
William Blair pointed to the high rate of discontinuations among participants taking pelacarsen as “one major caveat.” In HORIZON, 1,462 patients (35.1%) given 80-mg pelacarsen every four weeks prematurely discontinued treatment, the analyst said, vs. 761 (18.3%) given placebo on this timeframe.
But even with the discontinuations out of the equation, the drug still failed. For patients treated with uninterrupted pelacarsen, 167 or 11% had a MACE event vs. 204 or 10.1% in the placebo group, according to the subgroup analysis.

“This discontinuation rate is higher than we expected heading into the Lp(a)HORIZON readout and may have censored data impacting the primary endpoint analysis,” William Blair said.
Novartis and Ionis revealed in September that the trial failed to meet the primary endpoint of lowering the risk of MACE vs. placebo but did not provide details at the time.
The revelation shook Novartis’ stock amid several other clinical stumbles, with the market damage spreading to Lp(a)-targeting peers Amgen and Eli Lilly. It also raised questions about the value of targeting Lp(a) in cardiovascular disease (CVD). Amgen’s olpasiran and Lilly’s lepodisiran are both siRNA therapies that lower Lp(a) expression.
“We do see meaningful risk to a potential future in Lp(a)-driven CVD trials in light of results from Lp(a) HORIZON,” William Blair said at the time.
Upon seeing the detailed results, Leerink Partners lowered the probability of success for olpasiran from 50% to 20%. “[W]e are not lowering odds to 0% because it has a different structure and mechanism,” they wrote in a note to investors on Saturday, adding that Amgen’s drug “drives deeper Lp(a) lowering.”
William Blair had previously modeled sales of $710 million by 2030 for olpasiran but has now removed these estimates from its updated model. “[W]e still struggle to find confidence in olpasiran based on the totality of data presented,” the firm wrote on Monday.
Even when looking at the secondary prevention setting—in patients with established CVD—“there was no apparent difference in total events between participants randomly assigned to pelacarsen or placebo,” the NEJM Evidence authors wrote.

William Blair spoke specifically to this point, writing, “With no demonstration of efficacy in these high Lp(a) reduction subgroups . . . we believe it will be challenging for future studies to demonstrate benefit in secondary prevention in an otherwise well-controlled population.”
For now, the Lp(a) field will have to wait to learn more about whether this approach is viable. The Phase 3 OCEAN(a) study of olpasiran is set to read out topline data in early 2028, while Lilly is anticipating initial data from lepodisiran’s Phase 3 ACCLAIM-Lp(a) trial in March 2029.
For Novartis, the public reminder of pelacarsen’s failure couldn’t come at a worse time. Last week, the company confirmed nine reported cases of tumors in patients treated with its spinal muscular atrophy treatment Zolgensma, including two cases where that have been linked by evidence to the gene therapy. The FDA on Friday announced an investigation into the risk of tumor formation associated with the therapy.
And these headlines follow a summer of cascading challenges for Novartis. In September, the antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate del-desiran failed in a Phase 3 trial to significantly improve hand function in patients with myotonic dystrophy type 1, calling into question the company’s $12 billion buyout of Avidity Biosciences last year.
Then in late August, news broke that Novartis had paused a clutch of Phase 2 trials for the CAR T cell therapy rapcabtagene autoleucel after three patient deaths.

COLOGNE, Germany — Norway’s Kongsberg Maritime is pitching an unmanned fishing vessel design converted with technology to spot Russian submarines in the Arctic region on behalf of the British Royal Navy.
The company’s Arctic Hunter concept involves an industry-standard 56-meter trawler design with its fish-processing innards ripped out and replaced with autonomy features, allowing the craft to comb the ocean unattended for roughly 60 days at a time, a company spokesman told Defense News.
The ships would carry submarine-hunting sonar technology made by Thales UK, as well as secure communications capabilities, Kongsberg Maritime said in a Nov. 9 announcement. Some aspects of the ship, like the propeller, are slated for redesign to reduce its acoustic signature to avoid interfering with the onboard sonar, according to the company.
The proposal responds to a U.K. requirement for unmanned vessels that can assist anti-submarine warfare. The envisioned British Type 92 ships, as they are known in Royal Navy nomenclature, harken back to a World War 2-era idea that saw large numbers of relatively inexpensive converted whaler-type vessels protect U.K. warships against Nazi Germany’s submarine fleet.
Kongsberg Maritime’s concept of operations for the Arctic Hunter involves a flotilla of 10 ships based and supported somewhere “west of the Bear Gap,” a stretch of the Arctic Ocean between Svalbard and Norway through which Russian submarines must cross on the way to the open Atlantic, a company spokesman said.
Locating the drones’ hub near their area of operations beats having to travel the distance all the way from Britain, the logic goes.
The future Type 92 vessels are central to the British idea of a hybrid Navy with crewed and uncrewed ships working in concert on specific tasks. In anti-submarine warfare, surface drones like Arctic Hunter would assist future Type 26 frigates, being built by BAE Systems for the U.K., Australia, Canada and Norway, in their missions.
Kongsberg Maritime, recently incorporated as its own entity from the parent Kongsberg defense firm, says it understands the task of developing ships for Britain’s hybrid Navy as a “maritime engineering” problem rather than a naval armament problem, a company spokesman said. That’s because the commercial world already has plenty of hardy, proven ship types suited to harsh North Atlantic conditions that simply need to be retooled for unmanned operations.
If picked to build Type 92 ships, Kongsberg Maritime says it would do so in the United Kingdom.

source_document.body:
Twelve marketed drugs, including Eli Lilly’s and Novo’s weight loss mega-blockbusters, will require a label change under the new FDA update.
The FDA is requiring a labeling update for all approved GLP-1 receptor agonists, including products from Eli Lilly and Novo, to include a potential increased risk of a rare eye condition that can lead to vision loss.
The class-wide label change will involve adding a mention of non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), a serious eye condition that causes optic nerve swelling and can lead to blindness, often in one eye. With cases of NAION reported for all currently marketed GLP-1s, the FDA has concluded that the drug class is associated with a potentially higher risk of developing the condition and ordered all GLP-1 makers to update their labeling, according to a Monday release .
The agency listed 12 approved drugs that will have to make the change. These include Novo’s semaglutide drugs Wegovy and Ozempic and the heavy hitters in Lilly’s tirzepatide franchise, Zepbound and Mounjaro, plus the oral Foundayo.
“We see limited risk to our obesity coverage (specifically NVO/LLY) given rarity in incidence,” BMO analysts wrote in a Monday note. “The FDA’s action formalizes a previously recognized NAION safety signal, with low absolute event rates and a Warnings and Precautions update rather than a restriction on approved indications.”
The new regulatory change is based on an FDA assessment launched after a 2024 study published in JAMA Ophthalmology found an association between Novo’s semaglutide and higher risk of NAION.
The FDA performed a meta-analysis of 126 clinical trials across development programs, with 78,217 patients receiving a GLP-1 receptor agonist (RA). The agency “identified 15 probable NAION events, 10 in patients treated with GLP-1 RAs, five in patients receiving placebo, and none in patients who received other non-GLP-1 RA glucose-lowering medication.”
In other words, the analysis demonstrated a NAION incidence rate of 6.4 events per 100,000 patient-years for those treated with GLP-1s, compared to 3.8 events per 100,000 patient-years for comparators.
An FDA-run retrospective study using the agency’s real-world evidence data network examined NAION incidence among adults with type 2 diabetes taking medication and found no higher risk for NAION tied to GLP1s compared to SGLT-2 inhibitors, such as Boehringer Ingelheim and Eli Lilly’s Jardiance. However, the agency did identify an increased risk of NAION associated with GLP1s when compared to DPP-4 inhibitors, such as Merck’s Januvia.
The regulator also examined reports of NAION among GLP-1 users received through its adverse event monitoring system but said the reports were difficult to interpret because the disease’s risk factors often overlap with conditions commonly reported in patients treated with GLP-1s.
An FDA analysis of animal data failed to identify a mechanism for how GLP-1s could raise the potential risk of the eye condition.

Toyota now offers three fully electric SUVs: the bZ, C-HR, and bZ Woodland. Here’s how they stack up.
Toyota is getting in the EV game
After introducing the new and improved bZ (formerly the bZ4X) in late 2025, the electric SUV quickly became one of the most popular EVs in the US.
In the first nine months of 2026, it was the fourth-best-selling electric vehicle , behind the Hyundai IONIQ 5, Tesla Model 3, and Tesla Model Y.
With two additional electric SUVs now on sale, the CH-R and bZ Woodland, Toyota has suddenly become one of America’s top-selling EV brands.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Its EV sales have nearly tripled this year. According to Cox Automotive, Toyota ranked as the third most popular EV brand behind Tesla and Rivian in the third quarter.
Toyota offers three distinct electric vehicles: the 2027 bZ, C-HR, and bZ Woodland, each designed for different lifestyles, so which one is the best fit for you?
2027 Toyota bZ (Source: Toyota)
Toyota bZ
After launching the updated model last year, the 2027 bZ starts at $34,980. With the $1,595 delivery fee, the starting price is $36,576.
That’s for the standard 2027 Toyota bZ XLE FWD with an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 236 miles. For longer range, you can upgrade to the FWD Plus model, which offers up to 314 miles and starts at $37,980 (excluding the delivery fee).
The Toyota bZ is available in XLE and Limited grades, with front- or all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrains.

Two battery options are offered: The 57.7 kWh battery on the standard XLE FWD provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 236 miles, while the larger 74.7 kWh battery provides up to 288 miles of range on the XLE AWD and 314 miles on the XLE FWD Plus model.
FWD models produce either 165 hp (XLE FWD) or 221 hp (XLE FWD Plus and Limited FWD), while AWD models deliver a combined 338 hp.
The 2027 bZ also has a built-in NACS port, so you can use Tesla Superchargers without needing a separate adapter. Toyota said it takes around 30 minutes to charge the battery from 10% to 80%.
Inside, the 2027 bZ features Toyota’s updated cabin design. The setup features a 7″ LCD customizable Multi Information Display (MID) and a new 14″ Toyota Audio Multimedia display screen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.
The bZ is essentially designed as an everyday driver with a long driving range, modern tech, and available AWD.
2027 Toyota bZ Woodland (Source: Toyota)
Toyota bZ Woodland
For those looking for a bigger, more rugged option, the 2027 bZ Woodland may be a better fit. The Woodland is 6″ longer than the standard bZ and comes with standard AWD.
The longer body opens up more interior space, with up to 74.3 cubic feet of storage compared to the bZ with up to 67.1 cubic feet.
2027 Toyota Woodland electric SUV (Source: Toyota)
Unlike the bZ, the Woodland model has a standard AWD powertrain with Toyota’s X-Mode control system.
The setup delivers a combined 375 horsepower, 37 hp more than the standard bZ, making it Toyota’s most powerful EV currently.

It also adopts a more commanding, upright stance with 8.3″ of ground clearance and 3,500 lbs of towing capacity.
Although it uses the same 74.7 kWh battery as the standard bZ, the Woodland’s EPA-estimated range drops to 281 miles because of the added weight and power. Upgrading to the optional all-terrain tires sacrifices even more range, with up to 260 miles.
Like the bZ, the Woodland also has a built- in NACS port. Charging the battery from 10% to 80% takes around 30 minutes.
Inside, the bZ Woodland features the same 7″ LCD customizable Multi Information Display (MID) and 14″ Toyota Audio Multimedia display screen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.
The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380. All variants include standard roof rails, Dual Qi-capable wireless device chargers, heated front seats and steering wheel, and Digital Key capabilities.
2027 Toyota C-HR (Source: Toyota)
Toyota C-HR
Last, but not least, the C-HR is a smaller, sporty, coupe-like electric SUV. The 2027 Toyota C-HR starts at $37,080, or $2,100 more than the standard bZ.
It’s about 6.7″ shorter than the bZ, with a smaller wheelbase, but also comes with standard AWD. The dual-motor AWD setup delivers a combined 338 hp, not quite as much as the bigger, more powerful Woodland.
2027 Toyota C-HR XSE (Source: Toyota)
The C-HR is available exclusively with the 74.7 kWh battery, which provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 287 miles for the SE grade with 18″ wheels.
Upgrading to 20″ wheels adds a street-ready look but offers slightly less EPA range, with up to 273 miles.

The coupe-like design adds a sleek look and opens up interior space, with up to 59.5 cubic feet of rear cargo space when the rear seats are folded. That’s slightly more than the bZ, which offers up to 56.9 cubic feet.
Inside, the C-HR features the same setup as its other EVs, including a 7″ slim driver’s display and 14″ central infotainment screen.
Like Toyota’s other electric SUVs, the C-HR has a native NACS port. Charging the battery from 10% to 80% takes about 30 minutes.
The 2027 Toyota C-HR EV is available in two trims: SE and XSE. Standard features include two wireless Qi phone chargers, low-profile roof rails, Fabric/SofTex-trimmed seating, heated front seats and steering wheel, Toyota Safety Sense 3.0, and a power liftgate.

EICMA 2026 • Yamaha Births New Adventure Scooter Family, Three RW Models That Look More Like Motorcycles
One-Owner 1963 Plymouth Fury Ragtop Sat 20 Years in a Barn, 140k-Mile Poly V8 Can Still Do a Burnout
64 photos
Photo: YouTube/Rocket Restorations
1963 was how long ago? SIXTY-THREE years? Already?!?! Boy, and here I was, looking at brass-era cars and thinking “So, that’s how cars looked like 50 years ago.” Time has a bad habit of speeding up as it gets closer to the finish line, doesn’t it? Well, this one-owner Plymouth Fury could beg to differ – its past decades haven’t been exactly in a hurry to get it anywhere. Now it finally got a well-deserved, long-awaited resurrection.
Introduced for 1956 as a high-performance sub-series of the Belvedere, the Plymouth Fury became a standalone model line from 1959 through 1978 across seven distinct generations. The moniker rode on full-size body-on-frame chassis through 1959, full-size unibodies from 1960 to 1961, intermediate B-body platforms from 1962 to 1964 and 1975 to 1978, and full-size C-body architecture from 1965 to 1974, peaking in 1969 when fuselage C-body production approached 367,000 units.
Restyled on a 116-inch B-body wheelbase for 1963, midsize Plymouth production reached 244,395 cars, split between 158,612 V8s and 85,783 six-cylinders, though Chrysler kept no transmission totals by trim. The Fury series accounted for 67,584 vehicles, comprising 31,891 four-door sedans and 13,832 two-door hardtops in six-cylinder and V8 forms, plus 11,877 four-door hardtops, 5,221 convertibles, 2,352 six-passenger wagons, and 2,411 nine-passenger wagons with V8 power, alongside 15,319 V8 Sport Furys.
Buyers in 1963 paired a standard 3-speed column-shift manual, an optional pushbutton 3-speed TorqueFlite automatic, or a mid-year 4-speed manual with a 145-hp 225 Slant-Six, a 230-hp Polyspherical 318 V8, a 265-hp 361-cubic-inch V8, a 330-hp 383 V8, or the 415-hp/425-hp 426-cubic-inch Max Wedge V8.
Photo: YouTube/Rocket Restorations Base pricing spanned from $2,563 for the six-cylinder Fury four-door sedan to $3,071 for the nine-passenger wagon and $3,082 for the Sport Fury convertible. Standard V8 Fury convertibles carried a $2,924 base price, including one example scheduled for assembly in Detroit, Michigan, on December 24, 1962, and shipped to Chrysler City, Inc. in Portland, Oregon. This red relic who ended up with the short stick, and was relegated to bird toilet duties for way too long.
Optioned with a $162.10 Basic Radio Group, a $49.75 Sure Grip differential, $47.58 for 7.50x14 whitewall tires, a $21.55 tinted windshield, an $11.80 dual-jet washer, $5.60 for antifreeze, and a $157 destination charge, its factory window sticker reached $3,379.38. In 1963, that was quite the investment. Consider this: that year, the same amount would buy you a 409-Impala. The dual-quad, 400-hp version.
Because this red drop-top paired its 230-hp 318-cubic-inch Polyspherical V8 with a column-shifted 3-speed manual transmission , manual steering, and manual drum brakes, showroom shoppers ignored it for eight months. On August 22, 1963, Pacific Trailways bus driver Donald H. Richardson offered cash with no trade-in, securing a $667.18 discount to buy the convertible for $2,712.20 plus $12 in license and title fees. That’s what I call a deal – 20% off in the blink of an eye.
Photo: YouTube/Rocket Restorations Richardson immediately put the Plymouth to work, affixing a Dymo label with his name and employer to the inside mirror and paying $15.44 for three Safety King seat belts. Invoices preserved in his original folder chronicle a trailer hitch and tachometer installation at Armory Automotive Service in Portland at 654 miles, a clutch adjustment at Dalton Motors in Sacramento, California, at 1,430 miles, and replacement rear quarter trim in 1965.
In 1972, Richardson moved the convertible to a farm, a mile outside Pomeroy, Washington, where the dry climate protected its floor pans, rocker panels, and convertible torque boxes. Over the following decades, he installed dual exhaust tailpipes for $25.08 in 1984, rebuilt the front suspension in 1988, paid $333 for a black top in January 1989, and had Motor Works, Inc. overhaul the engine at 109,851 miles in February 1993.
Richardson drove the Fury another 30,733 miles to reach 140,584 total miles, fitting a bumper flag bracket for parades and registering Washington Collector Vehicle plates in October 2010 before passing away in 2022 after 59 years of ownership. After the car sat idle for nearly four years, Tom Hergert, front man and head wrencher of the Rocket Restorations YouTube channel, bought it from Richardson's daughter Sheila and sent his brother, Gary Hergert, to retrieve it.
Photo: YouTube/Rocket Restorations Following a five-hour drive (each way) to Pomeroy, Gary winched the Plymouth from an open farm shed where birds roosting on an overhead beam had buried the lowered top and red vinyl split-bench interior under thick droppings. Joined at the shop by assistant Evan and chief mechanic Jamie Attwood (himself host of his own Dead Dodge Garage YouTube channel), Tom vacuumed mouse carcasses from the cabin and scrubbed the driver's seat clean.
Taking charge of the mechanical revival, Jamie Attwood topped off the brake master cylinder and pumped the brake pedal enough times to call it a leg day workout, until hydraulic pressure returned. After connecting a fresh battery and watching the dashboard ammeter dip to confirm ignition continuity, he sampled the fuel tank behind the rear license plate, replaced a cracked rubber fuel hose, added half a gallon of coolant, and primed the two-barrel Stromberg carburetor with gasoline.
On the first turn of the key, the 318-cubic-inch V8 fired immediately and idled smoothly on old gasoline while the headlights, windshield wipers, and Conelrad AM radio came back to life. Hergert drove the Fury onto the grass to wash off decades of filth before a sudden rainstorm forced the crew to lift the power top manually, after which he unbolted two homemade trunk plates hiding huge rodent nests.
Photo: YouTube/Rocket Restorations After vacuuming the trunk troughs, pulling the lower quarter panel drain plugs on the shop lift, flushing the cavities with water, and soaking them in Lysol, the team tackled the mechanical leaks. While Evan wired a replacement passenger-side taillight socket, Hergert cured a severe engine oil leak by replacing a pinched oil filter adapter gasket and messy silicone sealant, spinning on a shorter Wix filter with fresh high-zinc oil.
To silence a noisy front end, Attwood removed the radiator and four-blade fan, transferred the heater hose thread adapter bushing into a new cast-iron MasterPro water pump, and installed a single-pulley alternator, fresh hoses, and a new V-belt. After testing the Sure Grip axle with smoky burnouts, Attwood test-drove the Fury at 50 mph on its first outing in 20 years before Tom Hergert takes the car back to the original owner’s wife, Sheila, to showcase the resurrected Mopar.
Having one owner its entire existence was a definitive plus for the classic, and having own that cared for it is probably why we got to see it brought back to life (play the two videos below for two original versions of the same revival) in such an expeditious manner. There are some minor details to address, such as the power top, or fresh tires, but the key elements are done for. If only all barn finds resurrections were this good…

MINI Aceman, Electric Cooper, and Electric JCW Recalled in China for Detaching Rearview Mirrors
95 photos
Photo: MINI / edited
Some battery-electric MINIs are manufactured in China as part of a joint venture between Great Wall Motor and BMW. That arrangement explains why this MINI recall involves only domestically produced models, which may lose their rearview mirrors under normal driving scenarios due to insufficient bonding.
Spotlight Automotive is the joint venture in question, and the expanded recall covers no fewer than 714 examples of the Aceman crossover, the full-electric Cooper , and zero-emission John Cooper Works models. The mounting bracket for the interior rearview mirror may not adhere properly, which means the mirror could obstruct the driver's view by loosening.
A complete detachment is also possible, but unfortunately, the manufacturer did not explain in the filing published by the SAMR who is to blame for this bonding defect. S2026M0113V is what the State Administration for Market Regulation calls this campaign, which expands on a July 2026 recall.
Spotlight Automotive's Zhangjiagang assembly complex is listed in the filing as the factory that produced the subject vehicles, with production dates ranging from April 7 through April 23, 2026, for the Cooper electrics. The JCW population was assembled between April 7 and April 10, 2026, while the subject Acemans were built from January 13 through April 23, 2026.
Rather than sticking the mirror back into place, mounting bracket and all, the remedy involves replacing the windshield. Spotlight Automotive tasked BMW Automotive Trading with replacing the assembly in full, and the filing published by the SAMR leaves a few questions unanswered.
Photo: MINI As noted earlier, the actual root cause remains unknown. The supplier of the adhesive and potential issues with the bonding process have not been detailed either, which is a bit uncanny if you ask me. Nevertheless, affected customers will have their vehicles fixed at no charge whatsoever.
Customers will be contacted by the folks at BMW China through registered mail, by telephone, and via SMS. In the meantime, customers may contact the automaker's local after-sales hotline for additional information. The Chinese State Administration for Market Regulation Recall Center is another option for them.
Internally referred to as J01, the full-electric MINI Cooper looks extremely similar to its dinosaur juice-drinking brother. They are completely different models underneath, though, and you can thank BMW's joint venture with Great Wall Motor for this huge difference beneath the sheet metal.
Back home in the United Kingdom, the most affordable Cooper E specification of the bunch will set you back 26,905 pounds sterling as opposed to 34,905 for the John Cooper Works. Both are front-wheel drive, and both offer relatively poor driving range. In the WLTP, their maximum estimates are 186 and 250 miles, respectively, meaning 300 and 402 kilometers in metric speak.
The Aceman crossover was developed on similar underpinnings, and you can't have it any other way than electric. For the Aceman E, prospective customers in the UK have to spend 29,060 pounds sterling at the very least. In return, they get a 38.5-kWh battery that promises no more than 192 miles (309 kilometers) on a full charge.

EICMA 2026 • Benelli Showed the World Its New Tornado Naked Tre 903 Concept at EICMA 2026 and It's a Triple!
Brabus 800 Shaves 0.1 Sec off the 0–60 Mph Over a Porsche Turbo S It's Built on, for Twice the Price
37 photos
Photo: Brabus
"My German ragtop sportscar isn't making enough power. Or isn't going fast enough. Or it's too slow off the line. Or something... CAN YOU DO SOMETHING ABOUT THAT? " said probably only owners who complained to Brabus about their regular Porsche 911 Turbo S, but didn’t get the BRABUS 820 from four years back. Guess what the German tuner did? Instead of calling a spiritual enlightenment coach to guide these speed-addled billionaires, the speed scientists in Bottrop grabbed their wrenches and built yet another 800-hp hair dryer.
Long before anyone decided that the 992.2 generation needed an 800-horsepower intervention, Brabus already possessed an irresistible urge to meddle with Stuttgart's crown jewel. Consider their previous exploit, the BRABUS 820 Cabriolet based on the 991.2 generation.
That machine took a standard 3.8-liter twin-turbocharged flat-six and extracted a blistering 820 hp and 950 Nm (700 lb-ft) of torque through custom turbochargers and ECU mapping, rocketing to 100 kph in 2.5 seconds and topping out at 340 kph (211 mph). It proved beyond all doubt that subtlety was merely a suggestion in the dictionary of Bottrop.
Yet time marches on, and factory engineers eventually caught up, introducing the latest 992.2 Porsche 911 Turbo S Cabriolet. Fresh out of Zuffenhausen with a base price of $284,300, this drop-top weapon packs a 3.6-liter twin-turbocharged 6-cylinder boxer engine assisted by a 400-volt T-Hybrid system.
Photo: Brabus With two electric turbochargers and an electric motor nestled inside its 8-speed dual-clutch transmission, the stock convertible produces 711 PS, or 701 hp, and 800 Nm. In imperial human terms, 800 Nm equals 590 lb-ft of instantaneous torque, fed by a compact 1.9 kWh battery and routed through all-wheel drive.
The standard Cabriolet rockets from 0 to 100 kph in 2.6 seconds, while the $270,300 Coupé takes 2.5 seconds and hits 200 kph in 8.4 seconds. Both reach 322 kph, or 200 mph, which is apparently pedestrian when you are late for a Monaco yacht party.
Naturally, Brabus looked at the most powerful production 911 in history and decided Porsche engineers were being exceptionally too humble about the capacity of their flat-six masterpiece. Enter the Brabus 800, a comprehensive conversion offered for both the Cabriolet and Coupé.
Photo: Brabus If you happen to be browsing their inventory, you will discover that this automotive fever dream commands a staggering price tag of €482,713.63 before local taxes. That’s about $540,757 in Legal Money of the United States. It is also about 200k Euros (225k USD) more than a factory Porsche. The good news is the coupe is only €419,580 ($470,000).
By installing the PowerXtra P36-800 performance upgrade onto the 3,591-cc flat-six engine, the tuner extracted an extra 65 kW, or 89 hp, pushing total hybrid system output to a glorious 588 kW, or 800 hp.
Peak torque simultaneously climbs by 100 Nm to a tectonic 900 Nm, or 664 lb-ft, ensuring the driver’s toupee reaches destination before the wearer does. That newfound muscle shaves 0.1 seconds off the factory sprint, launching the Brabus 800 Cabriolet from 0 to 100 kph in 2.5 seconds and the Coupé in 2.4 seconds. Top speed remains electronically capped at 322 kph, or 200 mph, with consumption at 11.5 l/100 km (20 mpg).
Photo: Brabus Because saving 0.1 seconds is meaningless if the neighbors cannot hear your financial superiority from two blocks away, Brabus swaps the standard titanium muffler for a valve-controlled sports exhaust system. Its quadruple rounded tailpipes sit seamlessly inside the rear diffuser, letting drivers toggle between a polite whisper and a volcanic boxer roar at the push of a button.
Emitting 261 g/km of CO2 never sounded so theatrical or mechanically intoxicating with the roof down. Speaking of carbon: visual subtlety was never on the menu either, yet the newly developed exposed-carbon aerodynamic package is genuinely brilliant engineering. Available in glossy or matte finishes, every component works in harmony with the factory active aerodynamics rather than just looking cool.
Up front, a carbon-fiber spoiler with raised side flaps reduces axle lift at high speeds, accompanied by bespoke carbon fascia inserts, vertical air intake louvers, and a complete carbon-fiber front hood. Along the flanks, carbon-fiber mirror housings and sculpted side skirt attachments visually stretch the widebody silhouette, making the car look like it is breaking speed limits while parked outside a café.
Photo: Brabus Out back, an elevated carbon-fiber rear spoiler teams up with the active wing system to pile on extra downforce, while a carbon-fiber rear diffuser and a carbon rear cover bearing raised Brabus lettering between the taillights finish the transformation . This rolling sculpture also marks the world premiere of the center-lock forged Brabus Monoblock ZL Platinum Edition wheels, featuring five pairs of delicate Y-shaped spokes finished in glossy black with polished surfaces.
Measuring 9.5J x 21 inches up front and 12J x 22 inches in back, they wear Continental SportContact 7 tires sized 255/30 ZR 21 and 335/25 ZR 22, tucked under height-adjustable sport springs lowering it by 25 millimeters (near as makes no difference one inch). Crucially, those adjustable springs are calibrated to work seamlessly with the factory active dampers, sharpening turn-in without turning your spine into a torsion bar over cobblestones.
Inside the cabin, the Brabus Masterpiece saddlery replaces almost every inch of standard trim with hand-stitched black leather accented by contrasting gray piping and a gray 12-o'clock steering wheel marker. The seats, floor mats, and trunk mat showcase intricate Dynamic Diamond Double quilting and perforations. Even the upper and lower dashboard, steering wheel airbag cover, center console, A-pillars, sun visors, and seat back panels are swathed in supple hide.
Photo: Brabus To remind passengers who built this cockpit, Brabus Signature Carbon adorns the dashboard, console, steering wheel, and doors. Aluminum pedal pads, an anodized footrest glowing with red Brabus lettering, and carbon-fiber sill plates with logos alternating between red and white complete this opulent bespoke interior makeover.
Did anyone on Earth genuinely need an 800 hp hybrid Porsche 911 Turbo S Cabriolet costing nearly 400,000 Euros? If they did, where exactly would they do 200 flat-out mph with the breeze hurricaning their hairline behind their ears? Then again, there’s a Chinese EV that just broke the 500-kph barrier (310 mph).
That is precisely why the Brabus 800 is such a triumph. Rather than ruining an icon with garish gimmicks, Bottrop elevated every dynamic, aerodynamic, and tactile metric with obsessive German precision. It is an outrageously fast, impeccably tailored masterpiece that turns a clinical Stuttgart supercar into an unapologetically wicked work of automotive art.
Which doesn't always mean going above, ahead, beyond what's behind. Brabus actually took a small step back, downgrading from the previous Porsche 911 Turbo S build to this 20-hp, 11 mph tamer, 800-hp rocket.

Processing facilities at Alphamin Resources’ Bisie tin mine in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Credit: Alphamin Resources
Posted By: Henry Lazenby November 9, 2026
Alphamin Resources (TSXV: AFM; JSE: APH) has agreed to supply a new U.S. smelter with tin concentrate from the Democratic Republic of Congo, diversifying its sales as Washington backs domestic minerals processing.
The initial two-year deal covers up to 3,600 tonnes of contained tin annually from Bisie, about 180 km northwest of Goma, the capital of North Kivu province. The material is destined for U.S. refiner Nathan Trotter & Co.’s $65-million (C$92 million) smelter in Virginia, which targets first production next year, Mauritius-based Alphamin said Monday.
“Alphamin has been actively seeking to diversify its customer base and to support the development of western tin refining capacity,” the company said in a release.
The allocation would account for up to 18% of Bisie’s targeted annual output, linking an established African mine to new U.S. processing capacity. For American manufacturers, the arrangement offers a potential source of tin for solder used in electronics and defence equipment.
Alphamin shares traded 6.6% higher at C$1.30 on the TSX Venture Exchange at noon on Monday, giving the company a market value of about C$1.7 billion.
US processing
Nathan Trotter is building its Tin Ridge facility in Henry County, Virginia. The project, announced in September 2025, is designed to process both tin concentrate and scrap and create an estimated 118 jobs at full capacity.
Alphamin didn’t disclose pricing, treatment charges or the expected date of first shipments. The company cautioned that construction and commissioning delays at the smelter could affect the arrangement.
The Pentagon awarded Nathan Trotter $19 million in 2024 to develop domestic tin processing.
Alphamin CEO Eoin O’Driscoll told commodities pricing agency Fastmarkets last month that about 70% of the company’s concentrate went to Yunnan in China, where competitive processing charges helped attract its business. Most of Alphamin’s concentrate would continue to go to China, he said.
Abu Dhabi-based International Resources Holding became Alphamin’s controlling shareholder in July 2025 after buying a 56% interest through its Alpha Mining subsidiary. IRH supports the U.S. supply arrangement, Alphamin said Monday.
Supply risks
U.S. processing would still depend on reliable shipments from eastern Congo. Alphamin halted mining and processing at Bisie on March 13, 2025, because of security concerns, then began a phased resumption of tin production on April 15.
Bisie produced 5,030 tonnes of tin in the quarter ended Sept. 30, broadly unchanged from the preceding three months and consistent with Alphamin’s annual guidance of 20,000 tonnes, the company reported Oct. 6. Alphamin indirectly owns 84.14% of the operating subsidiary; the production figures are reported on a full-mine basis.
Alphamin warned in that update that the fourth quarter is usually its most difficult period for logistics. It had mobilized additional trucks and fuel reserves to prepare for a potentially more disruptive rainy season.

EICMA 2026 • Triumph TF-E Bikes Get Even More Enduro With Updates for the 2027 Model Year
Don't Count on Tesla To Deliver Those $59,990 Cybertrucks, As Musk Foreshadows "Amazing Scarcity"
6 photos
Photo: Tesla
Elon Musk announced the demise of the Tesla Cybertruck while at the same time saying that a new shift will be added to its production line. He also said that Tesla "will have to return deposits to a lot of people." Given the recent price hikes and the fact that Tesla doesn't accept new orders on the base variant, it's almost certain that people who ordered it at $59,990 won't get their vehicles.
When Elon Musk turned his back on electric vehicles and Tesla's mission to electrify the transportation sector, he promised the change would bring "amazing abundance." It was March 2025, Musk was the acting DOGE chief, and Tesla sales suffered. As he has often done, Musk deflected criticism by announcing a new direction for the company, one that prioritizes robots, artificial intelligence, and autonomous driving.
More than that, Musk proclaimed that in a not-so-distant future, money would become irrelevant, precisely because robots would do all the work and people would just sit back and enjoy said abundance. Despite that promise, Musk did everything to ensure more money for himself, including a multi-billion compensation package.
Even more, he directed Tesla away from vehicle manufacturing because it did not make enough money and would needlessly consume Tesla's engineering and financial resources. He persistently bragged about trillions in potential revenue generated by Tesla's Robotaxi arm, as if money suddenly mattered again.
The Cybertruck is making money, but somehow disappoints Musk That's the background against which Musk announced that the Cybertruck would stop production in eight months. The announcement caused quite a stir in the Tesla community, even though the electric pickup truck sold in insignificant numbers. The Cybertruck's demise was long anticipated, yet the announcement sent ripples throughout the automotive industry.
The small sales numbers for a vehicle whose development likely cost billions hint at huge losses. However, Musk was quick to point out that the Cybertruck was still profitable. However, he said that building the Cybercab instead would create a lot more value for the company. Coming from the man who said money won't matter soon, this is strange.
Even worse, the way things turned out leaves little hope that those who ordered the cheapest Cybertruck variant would ever get their vehicles. In the same tweet, Musk announced that the Cybertruck's order rate far exceeds the production rate, and a lot of people won't get the vehicle they ordered.
This raises more questions, as Tesla published every quarter in its shareholder decks that the Cybertruck production line has an annual capacity of 125,000 vehicles. This means that it could theoretically build over 80,000 Cybertrucks in the remaining eight months until production stops. If this doesn't sound impressive, you should know that this is more trucks than Tesla has sold since delivery started in November 2023.
That's the same nonsense that Tesla has been fanning since the $59,990 Cybertruck variant went on sale in February. The company pushed delivery estimates into 2027 as if it already exhausted all production slots for 2026. However, as delivery numbers were reported quarter after quarter, we learned that Tesla never sold more than 8,000 trucks per quarter, versus the 30k-unit theoretical production capacity.
The $59,990 Cybertruck is as good as dead There's no reason to believe it will be any different this time. Despite Musk's pledge that Tesla will "try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months," we will undoubtedly see in the following quarters that Tesla only delivered a handful of pickups. Unsurprisingly, he tries to prepare us for this outcome, saying that Tesla "will have to return deposits for a lot of people."
You can argue that Tesla will still make some Cybertrucks, possibly even some of those elusive $59,990 AWD models. Fair point, but let's not forget that the company also raised the prices significantly just last week. Even the base variant, which you can no longer order, is listed with an $82,490 starting price. If you think Tesla would sell you that same truck at $59,990 just because you reserved one in February, I have a bridge to sell.
Even if Tesla does deliver the base Cybertruck AWD to some of the early reservation holders at the price they ordered, it will not make any efforts to prioritize them. In the best-case scenario, some lucky chaps will get their trucks so that they can brag about it on social media.
This actually happened already, with some having received their $59,990 trucks this summer, while others have been put on hold indefinitely. Meanwhile, more expensive variants of the Cybertruck had no restrictions.
This shows that Tesla is reluctantly selling the Cybertruck, and has been doing it all along. Production capacity hasn't been a problem, and the company is no longer constrained by Li-ion cell availability. Even when it promised a cheaper variant that appeared to be successful, it refused to actually build it, blaming huge demand and raising prices instead.
Prepare for a day when you won't be able to buy a Tesla The Cybertruck was not the first Tesla model to go to the graveyard of automotive history. The Model S and Model X were killed just a few months ago. These were also low-volume vehicles, and their demise was entirely justified. This means that Tesla is essentially selling only two vehicle models: the Model 3 and Model Y.
Both have grown long in the tooth, sharing a platform that debuted with the Model 3 in 2017. Despite a recent refresh, they have failed to catch up with Chinese rivals in terms of charging performance and battery tech. It might not matter much in North America. Still, in all other markets, Tesla is slowly but surely falling behind competition.
This has always been a recipe for disaster, and staying on this path will only mean that Model 3 and Model Y will soon disappear, too. That would be the end of Tesla's automotive business, if we don't count the Cybercab. However, the golden driverless car is unlikely to conquer the world despite Musk's optimism.
Even in the most optimistic scenario, the Cybercab will be confined to big cities in the US, with heavy regulatory constraints in other regions. Tesla couldn't push FSD in China, and it won't be able to sell the Cybercab there. Europe might be easier, but not with the current "move fast, break things" attitude. However, the vast majority of people on Earth will still want to drive their own vehicles, and Tesla won't have anything to offer them.

HMM has declared general average following the fire aboard the HMM Platinum , generating a slew of new hurdles for cargo owners, with the carrier still seeking a port of refuge for the vessel, which has spent the past month anchored off the South African coast.
Korhi Average Adjusters & Surveyors have been appointed to handle the adjustment for the 5,593 teu containership, with Korhi and Richards Hogg Lindley responsible for collecting general average security.
Those with cargo aboard will be required to provide salvage security and general average security before shipments can be forwarded or released, while uninsured cargo owners will be required to provide cash deposits, although the amounts have yet to be determined.
Given the extent of cargo damage and timetable for discharging containers remains unclear, the requirements add more uncertainty for forwarders and their customers with shipments aboard the vessel.
Fire broke out aboard the Liberian-flagged vessel on 6 October, while sailing from Kattupalli to Santos, with reports claiming that the blaze originated in a container while the ship was off Madagascar’s southern coast, with some 2,300 boxes aboard.
Salvage specialist SMIT was appointed under a Lloyd’s Open Form agreement, while the vessel diverted towards South Africa but finding a suitable port of refuge has proved complicated.
Ngqura has been identified as a possible destination, with Transnet National Ports Authority reportedly considering a request for the vessel to enter, but AIS data from Wingo Marine on 9 November placed the ship at anchor around 29km north-east of Durban.

The “super-luxury executive flagship sedan,” as BYD calls it, made its official debut in Abu Dhabi, UAE, over the weekend.
For those who don’t know, Yangwang is BYD’s ultra-luxury sub-brand, sitting at the very top of its brand hierarchy.

BYD said the “Golden Body Proportions” are designed to maximize interior space for both front and rear passengers.
Its meticulous front-end design is inspired by “Ding,” a traditional ancient Chinese cauldron, featuring “diamond-cut” headlights, a 137-gemstone dot-matrix grille, and, to top it off, a 24K pure gold car emblem sits up front and center.

Inside, the flagship sedan takes luxury up a notch with a massive, full-length panoramic center infotainment screen that extends from the driver to the passenger side.
BYD Yangwang Altior interior (Source: BYD)
The “Wrap-around cockpit” is designed to create an immersive, premium experience, with four executive seats and a central island for rear passengers that includes vehicle controls, storage, and even a champagne glass holder.
BYD said it offers the most second-row space in its class, but didn’t reveal specifics. The zero-gravity “cloud-like” rear seats feature a four-ball mechanical massage head, you know, for those longer trips.

The interior features premium materials, including full-grain genuine leather seats, diamond-cut detailing, real wood trim, and natural lambswool foot pads.

Maserati To Unveil Concepts Previewing the Next Levante and Quattroporte in December 2026
14 photos
Photo: Maserati
December 10, 2026. That's when the House of the Trident will purportedly debut a couple of concepts that are supposed to preview the next-generation Levante and Quattroporte.
This information comes from The Supercar Blog rather than Maserati. Neither concept has received official confirmation from the Modenese automaker. Be that as it may, we do know for certain that Stellantis gave its blessing to Maserati for two larger models.
As far as the Levante's replacement is concerned, everyone and their dog knows that Maserati needs a larger sport utility vehicle in the lineup. The Grecale simply does not cut it alone, especially in markets where bigger is better. Just like its predecessor, the new Levante will have to prove its mettle against BMW's X5, the Mercedes GLE, and the Porsche Cayenne.
The Quattroporte, meanwhile, would have to be less conventional than just another performance-oriented luxury sedan. Porsche already knows that such vehicles don't sell too well, but nevertheless, the German automaker is currently prepping a mid-cycle refresh of the Panamera.
During its FaSTLAne 2030 strategy announcement on May 21, 2026, the multinational automotive group confirmed that Maserati has two new E-segment vehicles in the offing. Technically speaking, E-segment means E-Class and 5 Series rather than a full-size luxobarge like the S-Class and 7 Series.
Photo: Maserati The group's announcement failed to identify either vehicle by name or disclose production dates. Given the aforementioned, the concepts reported by The Supercar Blog should not be treated as hearsay. If you ask me, the next Quattroporte deserves particular attention because of Santo Ficili.
Maserati's chief executive officer made it clear that a traditional sedan profile does not cut it, describing a low-slung vehicle that blurs the line between a shooting brake and a crossover. A rather unusual direction for the Quattroporte, but not entirely surprising. Toyota did it as well, replacing the sedan-bodied Avalon with the fastback-style Crown.
In any case, a Quattroporte with different proportions from its forerunners would attract new customers for the brand. The practicality of a larger cargo area would also make it more attractive. Combined with a higher seating position and some crossover touches here and there, Maserati could be onto something here.
That approach is a lot more interesting than simply responding to the S-Class and 7 Series, and Maserati has always had an easier time attracting attention when it does something different. The Levante has less room for experimentation, though, because mid-size luxury sport utility vehicles are very hot as of this writing.
Back in January 2024, the company outlined a product strategy built around electric-only successors for the Levante and Quattroporte, models that would have debuted in 2027 and 2028 . Considering that Maserati canceled the development of the MC20 Folgore in March 2025, chances are the new Levante and Quattroporte will offer internal combustion and hybrid options.

The acceleration of the energy transition in recent years has pushed the renewable energy market into a new phase of its journey. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), renewables are now relied upon to provide more than a third of the world’s power (and growing), as global narratives around clean energy shift away from net zero toward energy security and resilience.
With renewable energy portfolios increasing in scale and sophistication to meet this need, and the market facing a cocktail of new challenges, the role of the asset manager is fundamentally changing.
1. A single renewable energy power generation site can now combine wind, solar, and storage, each adding its own layer of technical and commercial complexity. Source: Power Factors
Specifically, they must adapt to blend their technical and commercial expertise with a strong understanding of how portfolios are performing across diverse technologies (Figure 1) and geographies. They must also find ways to navigate external pressures such as extreme weather, geopolitical uncertainty, shifting energy demand, and the downstream effects of supply chain bottlenecks.
While physical generation and storage infrastructure has rapidly progressed, adoption has lagged behind for the operational and digital infrastructure needed to ensure the highest levels of performance and revenue. Today’s new breed of renewables asset manager needs an upgraded toolkit, including artificial intelligence (AI)-powered solutions—discerningly—to keep pace with market demands and meet the changing expectations of their role.
Expanding Role of the Asset Manager
There was once a time when asset managers were primarily technical experts, their main priorities being to track energy production, supervise performance ratios and asset availability, and analyze the root causes of issues impacting generation. This role remains critical and has become more demanding, now that portfolios have evolved greatly in capacity, technology type, and geographical location. The technical expertise of asset managers is spread much more thinly today than ever before as they strive to manage diverse assets pumping out disparate streams of data. A small portfolio might pull from 10 to 30 data sources; a larger one can mean managing 50 to 200.
However, commercial and financial attributes are just as important as technical attributes for asset managers today as they manage a wider array of contracts and grapple with multiple potential revenue streams. Across an asset’s lifespan, the asset manager is responsible for meeting all kinds of contractual agreements, whether that’s an original equipment manufacturer warranty for the early stage of operational life, a power purchase agreement (PPA) to deliver an agreed volume of clean energy, or an insurance policy to mitigate catastrophic risks.
2. Generation and storage now share the same fence line, and increasingly, the same set of commercial decisions. Source: Power Factors
Meanwhile, the rise of battery energy storage systems (BESS) has increased the number of revenue options available for owners to pursue as renewable energy services expand beyond purely generation (Figure 2). The same battery might earn more through arbitrage, ancillary services, or capacity payments depending on the day and market, and cycling it harder to chase that revenue can accelerate degradation, turning “maximize revenue” into “maximize lifetime value.” Even the underlying contracts are evolving to keep pace. A PPA increasingly pairs generation with a separate tolling arrangement for storage, rather than acting as one fixed agreement.
This shift is turning the asset manager from a solo operator into an orchestrator. Their job increasingly means connecting operations and maintenance teams, commercial functions, and owners and investors, and making sure the right information reaches the right people in time for decisions to be made. The technical work hasn’t gone away; it now sits alongside a coordinating role that didn’t exist in the same way before.
That orchestration role carries real financial weight because the profitability of a portfolio depends on the asset manager’s ability to navigate the changing economics of technical, commercial, and financial performance. At the same time, this job has become more complex due to wider market challenges.
Although renewable energy assets thrive in locations of high irradiance or abundant wind, their resilience against increasingly extreme weather in recent years has been sorely tested. As the global renewables footprint has grown, assets have been more exposed to the elements, and destructive weather events like hail and lightning have caused major losses, forcing asset managers to move faster on damage assessment, insurance claims, and repair prioritization when severe weather hits.
Beyond extreme weather, day-to-day asset management continues to be affected by supply chain bottlenecks that have delayed critical maintenance, repair, and replacement work at great expense; by exploding demand for power as the data center boom gathers momentum, straining grid capacity and complicating how assets are dispatched; and by geopolitical tensions that have caused more volatility in the energy market.
Upgrading the Toolkit
In a market developing at an unprecedented pace, asset managers need ways to make sense of a potentially overwhelming data avalanche. The industry has seen an opportunity with AI-powered solutions to cut through the background noise and extract the data that informs truly value-generating asset management decisions. Increased automation also frees asset managers to focus on the tasks that require their unique expertise.
This ambition is justifiable, but the reality is that while generative AI tools add quite a lot of value in isolated areas, such as summarizing contracts and compliance documents or basic reporting, they lack the foundational context of renewable energy operations to deliver the kind of competitive advantage that today’s asset managers are seeking. Their inability to speak the language of renewables means that these models are more likely to create challenges for asset managers rather than alleviate them.
When we talk about upgrading the toolkit for asset managers to meet today’s exacting expectations for operational growth, we must focus on solutions that actually empower teams to do their best work, rather than introducing new constraints. To connect the technical, commercial, and financial considerations that unlock new value, the AI tools the industry adopts must provide accurate insights that are transparently verifiable. This is the difference between an evidence-based solution and one based on a best guess.
To credibly integrate AI into renewable energy asset management, the model has to be native to the domain in which it is providing support. We trained Unity REMI, Power Factors’ renewable energy management intelligence engine, on operational data from more than 310 GW of renewable energy assets globally, shaped by a decade of domain expertise working alongside renewable energy operators. Embedded in the Unity renewable energy management suite, REMI understands the specific context of every asset it supports so it can act on evidence, not assumptions.
This is crucial because what is commonly overlooked in the goal to optimize operations is the importance of optimizing the role of the asset manager. Discerning use of credible AI-powered systems—rather than time wasted verifying the outputs of an in-house or generic model—can provide the foundation for asset managers to identify and double down on the unique value that sets their portfolio apart.
Consider an asset flagging an unexpected performance dip. A generic AI tool might suggest a likely cause, but the asset manager still has to verify it against the specific turbine, weather pattern, or contract terms involved. A domain-native system checks that context automatically, separating the roughly 20% of signals that actually require action from the 80% that don’t, freeing the asset manager to make the call on whether to dispatch a technician or file a warranty claim.
3. Every enclosure here represents a live charge-or-hold decision, not a fixed output. Source: Power Factors
The same applies to more complex decisions. Facing curtailment, should the battery charge, hold capacity for an ancillary-services opportunity, or meet a PPA obligation, and what does each choice cost in future revenue (Figure 3)? A domain-native system surfaces those trade-offs in one place, instead of the asset manager piecing them together from separate tools.
As the complexity of the market deepens and the gap between technological and operational sophistication widens, the new breed of asset manager needs more than quick- fix solutions to make their current job easier. They need a trusted platform that supports them as both operator and orchestrator, empowering them to focus on connecting the people and information their portfolio depends on, and to find their competitive edge within a fast-changing industry.
—Deborah Beatty is chief strategy officer for Power Factors .

PARIS — Dutch startup Optics11 is in talks with dozens of navies about using its optical-fiber sensing technology for underwater monitoring and threat detection, with between five and ten navies already signed on as clients, Chief Executive Officer Paul Heiden said.
The company will have around 35 paid trials this year with navies testing its tech, Heiden told Defense News at the Euronaval maritime-defense exhibition outside Paris on Nov. 4. Those tests include several for the German Navy through various local defense-prime partners, as well as for Sweden, the United Kingdom, Belgium and France.
Optics11 beams light through optic fiber to detect acoustic vibrations underwater, either for static monitoring or towed array sensors, and Heiden said the technology is more sensitive and has higher resolution than passive sonar using piezoelectric detection. The firm is developing a towed array for the Royal Netherlands Navy for the future Orka-class submarines ordered from France’s Naval Group.
“Every navy knows that this is the technology of the future,” Heiden said.
The Optics11 portfolio includes OptiBarrier, a stationary seabed monitoring system, and OptiArray, a towed array that can be deployed from submarines and unmanned vessels.
Optics11 CEO Paul Heiden presents one of the company’s fiber-optic seabed monitoring systems on display at Euronaval near Paris on Nov. 4, 2026. (Rudy Ruitenberg/staff)
The CEO said Optics11 will probably raise funds next year, and do so at a unicorn valuation, referring to a startup valuation that exceeds US$1 billion. The startup raised around €100 million in funding in the past 15 months, through equity financing as well as €25 million in venture debt financing from the European Investment Bank, according to Heiden.
Optics11 is not yet profitable, and Heiden expects the company to become cash-flow positive in 2028.
The CEO said nearly everything around underwater data collection is “extremely secret” and a lot of information around navies using Optics11 technology is classified. He said the company’s products are currently deployed in war zones, “and yeah, I can’t say anything about that either.”
Optics11 has a technology lead in optical-fiber sensing after years of deep-tech research that would make it hard for a competitor to enter the market with anything similar, at least in markets including Europe, the Middle East and South East Asia, according to the CEO. He said he’s not sure where China or the United States stand in terms of developing similar technology.
The optical fiber technology used by Optics11 was initially used in medical applications, and is so sensitive it can detect cells dividing, according to Heiden. For underwater use, the company’s fiber-optic sensing can detect an oil tanker at 100 kilometers, the CEO said.
Most of the company’s “really crucial developments” of the past seven to eight years rely on trade secrets rather than patents to protect intellectual property, due to the sensitivity of the technology, Heiden said. The Dutch government provides specialists to help the firm protect its data, and vets company employees working on classified technology.
“You can’t publish this, you can’t patent it, so it all has to be kept secret, and we’re getting great help from the Dutch government to keep it truly secret,” Heiden said.
Heiden said he holds monthly discussions within the company to make sure employees disclose if, for example, they are being threatened or their families are being put under pressure.
The Optics11 strategy is to build and sell its products locally, both to reduce supply chain risk for customers and because governments want to see their defense investments flow back into their own economies. “We’ll identify who the local prime is, and then we’ll work with them to fully integrate our technology,” Heiden said.
Should Optics11 raise money next year, the funds would partly be used to finance its expansion in the Middle East and South East Asia, where the firm is opening offices and hiring staff with “the goal to operate in a highly localized manner.”
Optics11 already works with partners including Saab, Rheinmetall, Fincantieri, Thales and Exail, Heiden said. The firm is a technology supplier for Ocean Infinity, which was picked by the U.K. to manage the anti-submarine surveillance program as part of Britain’s Atlantic Bastion initiative.
The higher sensitivity of optical fiber compared to traditional sonar translates into a “much larger” amount of sensing data per cubic nautical mile, which Optics11 processes using its own edge-computing software, the CEO said.
“Initially I thought we could work with a partner, but our data density is so high that we couldn’t derive any value from third-party sonar processing software,” Heiden said. “That’s why we started building that kind of software ourselves, and it’s now an integral part of our offering. So we’ve really built a serious R&D operation here.”
Artificial intelligence has helped cut down the effort required to develop software, with Optics11 now employing ten developers, according to Heiden, who said that as recently as 2024 and 2025 he had still been planning for around 60 to 80 people in software development.
“That means you can invest that money in acoustic specialists who have a much better understanding of how sound travels through the ocean, which will allow you to optimize your algorithms much faster and make them more precise for sandy seabeds, rocky seabeds, that sort of thing,” the CEO said.
Optics11 has been working with the Royal Netherlands Navy for at least eight years, with the Dutch military providing millions of euros in subsidies, steering the direction of development, as well as testing the company’s technology on submarines, according to Heiden.
Attracting funding was still complicated for Optics11 in early 2024 due to financial firms excluding defense firms from investment portfolios, something which “completely changed” in November that same year after a vessel dragged its anchor in the Baltic Sea, severing several cables, Heiden said.
“All of a sudden all kinds of investment firms were willing to work with us,” Heiden said. “That was really driven by our ability to listen underwater, companies were prepared to seriously invest in that. So seriously, in fact, that over the last fifteen months we’ve raised about 100 million, which is quite a substantial amount.”
